summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted with acute right upper quadrant pain and nausea. Initial evaluation revealed gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening, and elevated liver enzymes, consistent with acute cholecystitis. A HIDA scan confirmed non-filling of the gallbladder. After failing conservative management, he underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy on hospital day three. Postoperatively, he developed transient urinary retention requiring a short-term catheter and mild postoperative ileus, both of which resolved. His white blood cell count normalized, and cultures were negative. Diuretics were held perioperatively and restarted before discharge. He recovered well, tolerated a regular diet, ambulated independently, and was discharged home on postoperative day six with follow-up arranged. His liver disease and HCC remained stable throughout the admission.
problems: Calculus of gallbladder with acute cholecystitis, without mention of obstruction
